item.title: Giants get timeline on Greg Newsome II injury with pressure now on Paulson Adebo
item.description: Greg Newsome II is going to miss more than just his revenge game.
item.content:encoded:
Greg Newsome II is going to miss more than just his revenge game.

Newsome is expected to miss at least the next four games and could be pressed to return before the end of the regular season after a high ankle sprain that requires tightrope surgery, The Post confirmed.

The Giants have seven games in seven weeks remaining. The high end of his timeline is six weeks on the sideline.

Access the Giants like never before

Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.

tRY IT NOW

Newsome has not yet been placed on injured reserve, which would sideline him for at least four games and create a roster spot needed to elevate practice-squad contributor defensive lineman Duane Smoot.

The Giants have now lost four defensive starters for long periods of time, including season-ending injuries to edge Brian Burns, linebacker Tremaine Edmunds and defensive lineman Chauncey Golston.

It makes Newsome’s recent decision to sign a three-year, $45.75 million contract extension rather than play out the rest of his walk year look wise. Had Newsome finished the season injured or playing at a lesser level through pain and then entered free agency, he might have been asked to accept another prove-it deal.

Without Newsome, the Giants will turn to benched former starter Paulson Adebo (four passes defended and an interception in place of Newsome against the Jaguars) to start next to Deonte Banks, who is having the best year of his career as he nears free agency. It’s a toss-up whether Banks or Newsome would be considered the Giants’ No. 1 cornerback as both have had shutdown moments this season.

Second-round pick Colton Hood, who has had a quiet rookie season, is first off the bench to play on the perimeter.

Newsome’s surgery is today, according to The Athletic.

item.title: Micah Parsons will make 2026 debut against Rams
item.description: Packers clear their star pass rusher in time for Wednesday
item.content:encoded:
The Green Bay Packers have activated Micah Parsons in time for Wednesday’s game against the Los Angeles Rams. It will be the star pass rusher’s first game since he tore his ACL almost one year ago in a loss to the Broncos on December 14. Parsons told the media on Monday that he was looking forward to facing the Rams and helping Green Bay make the playoffs if he was cleared to play, which is now the case.

“I’m so locked in on what’s ahead of me and I understand what this game Wednesday means to the organization and I myself and what it means for playoffs,” Parsons said. “And if I can be out there, I want to be out there and I’m excited for any time. Because we only got seven more games left, so I want to capitalize on all those if I can.”

Parsons had 12.5 sacks in 14 games during his debut season with the Packers after he was traded to Green Bay by the Dallas Cowboys in exchange for two first-round picks. Still only 27, Parsons has been on the Physically Unable to Perform list while rehabbing from a torn ACL.

He has never had fewer than 12 sacks in a season.

The Packers have the same 6-4 record as the L.A. Rams, meaning that Wednesday’s game is monumental in the hunt for a wild card spot in the NFC. The Rams could at least temporarily move into the 7-seed with a win over Green Bay. They’ll now have to contend with a motivated Micah Parsons in his first game in almost a year.

item.title: Fantasy football trade deadline strategy: Stop chasing floor. Chase upside
item.description: The fantasy playoffs are coming. Here are 10 players to target or move at the trade deadline, including Kenneth Walker III and Luther Burden III.
item.content:encoded:
It might sound counterintuitive, but with just a few more weeks left in the regular season, it's time to start trading for backups who largely haven't done much this season.

The reasoning here is that while you're dealing with byes and injuries during the regular season, having a WR5 who scores 5-8 points a game can actually be valuable. Five points is, as it turns out, more than 0. But in the playoffs, five points might as well be a 0. You're just not going to win many postseason matchups without being able to hit a ceiling.

So as you enter the last week or two or your trade deadline, you should feel fine about swapping high-floor, low-ceiling backups for bench stashes who haven't done much this year and are nothing but upside. Think backup RBs or WRs who might see more opportunity with an injury in front of them. These aren't going to end up being flashy trades, but if a star goes down and you have the backup, trading for him now could wind up as a league-winning move.

There are no teams on a bye this week, so you should have a full suite of players to debate. Here are 10 fantasy football trade targets for Week 12:

Week 12 fantasy football players to buy

RB Kenneth Walker III, Chiefs

Rookie Emmett Johnson has looked like a league-winner filling in for Walker the past two weeks, which might lower the veteran's value just enough to be able to buy him at the deadline. Johnson has played well enough to earn a consistent role even with Walker back, but it also seems unlikely that the Chiefs shy away from arguably the best running back in the NFL in September and October after he returns. If this mini-dip makes Walker available, you should pounce.

WR Luther Burden III, Bears

Burden's worst game of the season (two catches for 10 yards against the Saints in Week 11) came at a great time for those wanting to trade for Chicago's WR1. The Bears have an extremely easy schedule for fantasy to end the year and get the Bills, Packers and Lions in the fantasy playoffs (Weeks 15-17). Burden could be a WR1 to end the year and you can buy him as a WR2.

RB Sione Vaki, Lions

Outside of superstar Jahmyr Gibbs and quarterback Jared Goff, Vaki is the only Lions player to earn more than three carries this season. He has just 162 rushing yards this year, but if Gibbs were to miss any time, Vaki would immediately become a top-10 option at RB.

QB Cam Ward, Titans

Remember, we don't care if fantasy players score their points in the first quarter or in garbage time – and Ward has been crushing garbage time in November. With a schedule that ends with the Lions, Colts, Raiders and Steelers, he should continue to get opportunities to throw and close the season with weekly top-10 upside.

RB Chris Rodriguez Jr., Jaguars

Starter Bhayshul Tuten has an ankle injury that he continues to reaggravate, which could leave Rodriguez as not just a goal-line back, but an every-down player in one of the best offenses in the league.

WR Michael Pittman Jr., Steelers

I would not trade anything more than the bare minimum for Pittman, who hasn't played since Oct. 1 with a foot injury. He should return this week, though, and could become a more trusted safety valve for the ancient Aaron Rodgers than rookie Germie Bernard or DK Metcalf.

More: NFL power rankings Week 12: How far do Bengals fall after Monday's loss to Commanders?

Week 12 fantasy football players to sell

WR Antonio Williams, Commanders

The road to the playoffs is paved with talented, inconsistent rookie wide receivers who go from spike weeks to obscurity. We've seen it this year with Omar Cooper Jr., Germie Bernard and Caleb Douglas. There's a chance that Williams is the true, consistent breakout of his class, but after nine catches for 122 yards in Week 11, you should see if he can command a solid return at the deadline.

RB David Montgomery, Texans

The Texans' rush offense has been a mess for two seasons, while Montgomery had his best game of the year in Week 11 because Woody Marks was out with a concussion. With Marks likely back in Week 12, this backfield could get messy. Let someone else deal with the weekly headache.

WR DeVonta Smith, Eagles

Smith is back from a hamstring injury and hopefully has enough name recognition to fetch a return at the deadline. Fill-in quarterback Joe Milton has thrown for less than 170 yards in his two starts this year and we generally do not want to start WRs who have QBs throwing for pocket change every week.

RB D'Andre Swift, Bears

Even if Swift hadn't fumbled in Week 11 – which coach Ben Johnson has shown to not tolerate – the veteran still hasn't finished a game with more than four yards per carry since Oct. 11. Extreme touchdown luck has still made him a quality starter, but with Kyle Monangai finally back from a long toe injury, Swift could see his role really weaken over the next month.

item.title: Raiders gave Ashton Jeanty what he’s needed all season in breakout game vs. Broncos
item.description: If you want to know if Ashton Jeanty turned a corner Sunday in Denver, put yourself in Klint Kubiak’s shoes and take a look at the tape he broke down...
item.content:encoded:
If you want to know if Ashton Jeanty turned a corner Sunday in Denver, put yourself in Klint Kubiak’s shoes and take a look at the tape he broke down for his Raiders’ players Monday. 

Cue up the run that went for 46 yards. The first time through, take your eyes off Jeanty.

Watch the right guard. Watch the right tackle. Then run it back and watch Jack Bech, the receiver lined up in the left slot. Bech is a big part of how an eight-yard gain became a 46-yarder.

So, did Jeanty turn the corner? If he keeps getting the kind of help he got Sunday, yes.

The Raiders ran for a season-high 143 yards on 24 carries in their 38-24 loss to the Broncos, their best rushing total since the season opener. You have to go all the way back to Week 3 for the last time they ran for 100 or more yards.

They went into Denver averaging 70.7 rushing yards a game, 31st in the NFL. Jeanty beat that number himself with 79 yards on 11 carries. 

He added 90 through the air for 169 yards from scrimmage, the kind of afternoon the Raiders envisioned when they made him the sixth pick in last year’s draft. Put enough of those together and Offensive Player of the Year enters the conversation.

It also raises a fair question about how much of the blame for the first 10 games belonged on his doorstep. Go back to third-and-three at midfield. The Raiders trailed 17-0 in the second quarter. Before anybody could worry about springing Jeanty for 46, they had to get him three.

Start on the right side. Guard Trey Zuhn II adjusted to pick up blitzing linebacker Alex Singleton. Tackle DJ Glaze blocked down on Tyler Onyedim. Watch what that did for outside linebacker Que Robinson. For a beat, he had a clear path to the ball carrier.

Glaze could leave him there because he knew who was coming. Tight end Michael Mayer came in motion from left to right and buried Robinson. Inside, center Tyler Linderbaum turned D.J. Jones. Left guard Spencer Burford walled off Zach Allen, and left tackle Kolton Miller did the same to Dondrea Tillman.

There’s the hole.

Give Jeanty credit for seeing it and hitting it without wasting a step.

Now rewind and find Bech.

From the left slot, he immediately identified safety Talanoa Hufanga and took an angle that put him squarely between Hufanga and the runner. Freeze it as Hufanga comes into position to make the tackle. Bech gets to him at precisely that moment. Just inside that block, Zuhn is engaging Singleton.

Now watch Jeanty. He sees the second opening, cuts left off Bech and Zuhn and accelerates into open grass. According to NextGenStats, Jeanty hit a career-high top speed of 21.38 MPH. 

By the time Patrick Surtain II pushes him out of bounds, the Raiders are at the Broncos’ 4-yard-line.

Those last 38 yards are why a wide receiver’s block belongs in Kubiak’s lesson plan. But it all started with the communication and execution at the line of scrimmage.

It’s been a work in progress all year.

New scheme. Some new players.

And the new voices of Kubiak, offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko and offensive line coach Rick Dennison.

But for one Sunday, it all came together to offer a glimpse of what is possible.

“I just think over the season, as it’s gone on, our guys are getting more familiar and comfortable with the scheme,” Kubiak said. “And the more time on task that you have, you anticipate improvement, and it was a step in the right direction.”

Later that quarter, Fernando Mendoza got his turn to help. Jeanty ran a wheel route, Mendoza dropped the throw to him in stride, and Jeanty took it the rest of the way for a 68-yard touchdown. 

Twice before halftime, the Broncos had to chase the same running back to their goal line. 

The first time a receiver helped get him there. The second time he was the receiver.

Activation Jeanty was in full force. And it took everyone doing their job to turn him loose.

“Our offensive line played fantastic, as well as our running backs,” Mendoza said. “I think that’s a real threat. To have those guys rolling helps the offense tremendously.”

Jeanty’s other 10 carries produced 33 yards. Turn a couple of those into five-yard gains and consider what that buys Mendoza in his third NFL start Sunday in Cleveland.

Kubiak can call another run on second down. Mendoza can sell a play fake. And when a linebacker takes two steps toward the line of scrimmage, there’s room to throw behind him.

That’s the assignment for the Raiders. Give Jeanty enough room to make the first read. Stay on a block long enough to give him a second.

Then roll the tape one last time and watch what happens when a back with his vision and burst gets to make both decisions at full speed.

item.title: Chiefs sign OT Fred Johnson to 53-man roster
item.description: The Chiefs announced a pair of roster moves on Tuesday afternoon.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs announced a pair of roster moves on Tuesday afternoon.

They have signed offensive tackle Fred Johnson to their 53-man roster from the practice squad. Fullback Ben VanSumeren was placed on injured reserve in a corresponding move.

Johnson was released by the Eagles earlier this month and he signed to the practice squad in Kansas City last week. He played in seven games for the Eagles this season and 58 games for the team since the start of the 2023 season.

Right tackle Jaylon Moore is dealing with an ankle injury so Johnson gives them team experienced depth up front.

VanSumeren has a knee injury. He had five special teams tackles in six games this season.

item.title: Cowboys? Giants? 5 reasons to believe Commanders will win NFC East | Opinion
item.description: After a surprising and inspiring win over the Bengals, the Commanders are well positioned to make a run at the NFL East title, writes columnist Nate Davis.
item.content:encoded:
LANDOVER, MD – His wet, grass-stained uniform still clinging to him, Jayden Daniels stood transfixed in the bowels of Northwest Field. As reporters waited to ask him questions, the Washington Commanders quarterback watched from the dais of the stadium’s interview room as ESPN broke down the game-winning drive he’d just engineered in the final minute of his team’s prime-time upset of the previously scalding Cincinnati Bengals.

“My bad. What’s up?” Daniels said, snapping to following his team’s 22-20 triumph under the “Monday Night Football” microscope on Nov. 23.

Daniels’ emergence from his daze, ready again to meet the moment, might as well be a microcosm for a team that seems to be coming out of an early season hibernation – an uneasy slumber that’s been defined by close losses to good teams, injuries and, most prominently, misadventures navigating game-ending situations. But a more fully formed, suddenly awake Commanders team could be very bad news for the rest of an uninspiring NFC East field.

“Continue to stack (wins),” said Washington defensive tackle Tim Settle Jr. of a team that’s won three of four and has successive victories for the first time this season. “I feel like once we get this feeling, starts to be contagious.

“(T)his is the feeling we need in this locker room, especially around this time of the season.”

Indeed.

Here are five reasons Washington could very well be division champions and playoff bound when the regular-season dust settles on Jan. 10:

1. Jayden Daniels is back

No, he didn’t go anywhere. But injuries, this year and last, combined with early season struggles – particularly situationally – had tarnished some of the shine on the 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year. But he was ready for his national spotlight against Cincinnati.

Daniels’ 47-yard run on Washington’s opening drive of the third quarter set up a field goal and served as a reminder of his sublime dual threat abilities. His 335 rushing yards this season now lead all NFL quarterbacks.

“Their quarterback is a really explosive player” Cincinnati coach Zac Taylor said of Daniels. “He can make any throw on the field, so he’s very dangerous.

“We knew what we were dealing with when we came here, and they got the best of us today.”

But it was the frenetic final drive, Daniels ripping 22- and 42-yard throws to rookie wideout Antonio Williams over the final 46 seconds – and ensuring kicker Drew Stevens had sufficient time for the game-winning kick even though Washington had no timeouts left – that should engender hope that Daniels and a team two seasons removed from an NFC championship game appearance could be all the way back to form.

“I personally live for those moments, like high-pressure situations,” said Daniels, who hasn’t exactly risen to them previously this season. “Wanna go out there and make your mark on the game, obviously, and go.”

Said veteran running back Austin Ekeler: “Your star players gotta show themselves in the best moments, that’s exactly what happened there. … I’m expecting a lot more plays like that in the future.

COMMANDERS' NEW UNIFORMS: 'The Hail Raiser' invokes past mascot with spear logo

2. The defense is ascending

Quinn’s baby is growing up fast – and certainly showed its maturity on Monday by holding MVP frontrunner Joe Burrow and elite wideouts Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins largely in check.

Since a Week 7 bye, Washington hasn’t allowed more than 21 points in a game – after allowing at least 23 in its first six outings. The Commanders also have six takeaways over the past four weeks.

“We're a much better team than we were Week 1, Week 2, defensively,” said Quinn, who cited better tackling, pressure and communication as reasons for the improvement.

Burrow was on the verge of a league record after accounting for at least four touchdowns (passing/rushing) in his previous five games. He threw for two scores against Washington. Chase needed double-digit receptions to match Hall of Famer Calvin Johnson’s record of catching at least 10 passes in four straight games. Chase finished with five (for 31 yards).

“I feel like they had the utmost confidence in (their) offense, which they should. I mean, there's a lot of talented players on that side of the ball,” said Commanders pass rusher K'Lavon Chaisson, who was also proud of his unit for forcing a three-and-out after the Bengals won the coin toss to start the game and chose to receive the ball.

“I think we got the better of them today for sure.”

The Bengals had averaged 36.2 points over their previous five games and not fewer than 31 in any of them.

"I think guys are feeling confident," rookie linebacker Sonny Styles said.

"I think between the players and the coaches, that we're confident in our ability to be aggressive, to be on the offense and we're not gonna just gonna be on our heels and sit back. I thought we did that today. I thought we were aggressive. I thought we kinda dictated the terms out there today, so it was a good defensive game.”

3. Commanders rookies coming to life

Washington’s youngsters are coming of age and may have truly earned their stripes Monday.

Styles, the seventh overall pick from the draft, is quickly emerging as a fan favorite. The Swiss Army Knife defender had a season-high four pressures against Cincinnati and nearly picked off Burrow on the Bengals’ final drive, which would have precluded Daniels’ late-game heroics.

Williams had a breakout game with nine catches for 122 yards and could have the makings of a future No. 1 receiver given his fast-developing chemistry with Daniels, who likens the Clemson product to a younger brother.

Stevens also had his best performance to date, connecting on all five of his field-goal tries – including the game-winner – in suboptimal conditions while accounting for 16 of his team’s 22 points Monday.

NFL POWER RANKINGS: How high do Commanders rise?

4. Schedule breaks Washington’s way … statistically

The collective winning percentage of the Commanders’ remaining opponents is .417, making the remnants of their schedule the league’s third easiest and the most forgiving – by the numbers – in the NFC East. The Tennessee Titans, Arizona Cardinals and Atlanta Falcons are among the clubs that lie ahead, and Washington’s lone divisional game down the stretch is a home date with the Dallas Cowboys, who will have to play the division-leading New York Giants again.

Meanwhile, the Giants and Cowboys have the eighth- and ninth-most difficult remaining schedules league-wide, both lineups with at least a .550 win rate. And with the head-to-head tiebreaker against New York (6-3-1) in hand, the Commanders (4-5-1) need only catch the Giants and overtake the wildly inconsistent Cowboys (5-6) to be crowned.

5. Game-management issues are resolving

Quinn has been almost universally beloved by players for the duration of an NFL coaching career that spans nearly a quarter of a century. But his job security was most definitely a topic of discussion after botched clock management almost certainly cost his team a Week 5 home win against the Giants and seemed to resurface in losses to the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams. And whether those gaffes were definitively his fault, rookie offensive coordinator David Blough’s or Daniels’, everyone knows where the buck stops. And prior to playing the Bengals, the Commanders were 2-3-1 in one-score games this season. Chaisson described the mistakes as “trauma” for the team.

But Quinn and Co. seemed to be playing strategic chess Monday rather than being stymied by checkers.

Quinn opted for a go-ahead field goal on fourth-and-1 with 2:26 to play, rather than going for a first down, believing he could get the ball back to Daniels – and deny Burrow − for a final possession given the Commanders had all of their timeouts plus the two-minute warning. That strategy worked out, even though the Bengals retook the lead with its own field goal inside the final minute.

But Daniels went to work, ensuring his linemen got down the field so he could stop the clock after both of Williams’ big catches.

A clinical finish 😮‍💨

🔜 #WASvsAZ, 11/29, 4:25pm on FOX pic.twitter.com/486W4a1bQB

— Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 24, 2026

“They better bring their ass down there,” Daniels cracked. “They gotta get them miles per hour up.”

An edified Quinn said a heavy practice emphasis on those situations paid off.

“I think those scars help,” he said. “We spent a lot of time on (game-ending) situations. We continue to.

“But this was gonna be a back-and-forth game. I just knew it was gonna be punch, counter punch, punch, counter punch, based on who their weapons were.”

Daniels also had a look of gratification, especially after ingesting the ESPN replay prior to his news conference.

“Just you learn from mistakes, failures. You don’t let it define you, stick to the process,” he said.

“Go out there and just keep your head down and work.”

Seems like an approach that could take this team where it wants to go.

“Regardless of what happens, you can still have a chance at the end, right? The beginning of the season is not indicative of what you’re gonna go through the entire season, right? You can still climb yourself into position to get into the (playoffs),” Ekeler said.

“Yeah, we went through some ups and downs – still gonna go through ups and downs, that’s football. That’s the NFL. It’s not easy to win these games. Regardless, I think what Coach Quinn always talks about is us staying together, do it again, show up for each other, it’s about the team. As long we continue to have that mindset, regardless win or lose, we’re gonna put ourselves in position to have a good chance.”

Sure seems that way.

item.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: Hayden Winks' RB Blueprint for Week 12
item.description: Fantasy football analyst Hayden Winks lays out the blueprint for the RB position for Week 12.
item.content:encoded:
The Blueprint is my weekly column and basically everything that I use to build out the most accurate rankings I can. There will be this RB column, a WR column and a combination column on the onesie positions. You will find film notes and endless charts. Maybe enough charts to stress test the Yahoo website. I kid.

It's impossible to get every ranking thoroughly early in the week, so be sure to keep checking in on these columns through Sunday morning. As always, my full rankings at every position will be updated here soon.

1. Jahmyr Gibbs (vs. CHI) - 132.5 proj. total yards

Gibbs has recently finished as the RB5 and RB3 against the Vikings and Bucs, respectively, both defenses that sit at the top of every fantasy RB metric. There's no stopping this train.

The Bears defense is much better with DT Jeffery Simmons wreaking havoc, but Gibbs has shredded this defense for 100+ total yards in 4 straight games. Detroit enters as 2.5-point home underdogs with a 26.5-point implied total (sixth). Don't be surprised if his receiving volume ticks up here.

2. Christian McCaffrey (vs. SEA) - 88.5 proj. total yards

McCaffrey is a patriot. He's posted RB22 and RB14 outings outside of the states but is the RB2 on RB6 usage inside the country. CMC will play the rest of his games in the USA for those tracking at home. There's nothing new with his role or production. He's the RB3 this season thanks to his usual receiving role (RB4 in receptions per game) and the 49ers' truly dominant scoring offense.

Seattle will be a real test, just like the Vikings were last week. Seattle sits 24th in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields, and the Seahawks are fresh off a bye week. CMC was the RB11 with 83 total yards against them in Week 5 when the Niners won 32 to 29. He had 74, 57 and 142 scoreless yards against them in last year's matchups, too. It's reasonable to dock him for matchup reasons, but only so much. The 49ers dictate terms this year. San Francisco heads in as 3-point home favorites carrying a 25.25-point implied team total (eighth).

3. Kenneth Walker III (at BUF)

Update: Walker (groin) was a DNP on Monday's walkthrough.

Walker is going to be the very clear-cut lead back, despite Emmett Johnson doing a Bucky Irving impression as the interim starter. Patrick Mahomes, Andy Reid and everyone else with a brain knows this. That said, Walker may go from 23.3 touches per game down to 18-21 or so, now that they know what they have at RB2. That difference really doesn't matter much. He'll handle almost all of the goal-line role and has been excellent as a pass catcher, too.

The matchup is more mediocre. The Bills defense is coming alive in Year 1 of a new system, thanks to a trade at the deadline for a safety and a few breakouts up front. They're middle of the pack in most metrics, and the Chiefs are only projected for 23.25 points (13th) as field-goal dogs.

4. Bucky Irving (vs. CAR) - 94.5 proj. total yards

Irving has been fantastic since the end of September. He's been the RB5 on RB3 usage this past month, hulking 22.3 carries per game. Last week was another great outing, despite having an 80-yard TD called back for a rightful holding. Irving is the engine of the offense with the pass game completely broken for QB and WR reasons.

The Panthers are still poor stopping the run despite a DC change. They allowed Derrick Henry to go for 111 total yards and a score, and across the season Carolina is second-worst against the position. Irving hit them for 110-2 back in Week 7 (RB2) with RB18, RB41, RB5 and RB1 finishes in previous years. It's a great spot all around. The Bucs project for 23.25 points (13th) in a must-win game in the NFC South.

5. Javonte Williams (vs. PHI) - 88.5 proj. total yards

Williams is the RB8 on RB5 usage, riding the coattails of an amazing Dak Prescott season. He's easily leading the NFL in goal-line carries, and the Cowboys OL is one of the best. It's a great environment for fantasy points, that's for sure.

This week is no different. The Eagles traded away run-stopping DT Jordan Davis, placed All Pro LB Zack Baun on IR and won't have others on defense. It's a tanking defense that is now allowing 121 rushing YPG (12th most). Williams has already hit them for 155 total yards and a score this year back in Week 7, after finishing as the RB19 and RB3, respectively, against a better version of this defense in 2025. The Cowboys own a 28.0-point team total (fourth) on Thanksgiving as massive favorites.

6. James Cook III (vs. KC) - 98.5 proj. total yards

There is some serious weather expected here. Very cold rain with wind.

Cook sits as the RB9 in half PPR points per game on RB8 usage across his last four games. He leads the league with 23 carries per game in that span and has found the end zone on the ground in 4 straight contests. Nothing new here.

The matchup is an uphill one. Kansas City ranks 28th in half PPR points allowed to RBs, albeit with a fairly soft schedule so far. They did hold Bijan Robinson to RB13 a couple of weeks ago, for what it's worth. Offenses facing the Chiefs have attempted to run on them in neutral situations (league-low 46% neutral pass), and the Bills have the personnel to do that. Cook has had 125 and 134 total yards against the Chiefs in his most recent outings, respectively. Buffalo carries a 26.75-point implied total (fifth) as 3-point home favorites. I'm not adjusting too much for matchup.

7. Jonah Coleman (at PIT) - 93.5 proj. total yards

Coleman has completely dusted J.K. Dobbins, who had one snap in Week 11's blowout win. His vision is what stands out on tape. He knows when to cut back, find cheap yards and bounce it depending on the look. He's a pretty mediocre athlete, but Coleman will hit a ton of singles and doubles behind this quality OL and rushing scheme.

Jonah Coleman has very good vision. Going to be one of the better singles and doubles hitters. pic.twitter.com/JesVhyUioV

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 23, 2026

On top of that, Coleman is averaging 3.5 receptions per game this month with R.J. Harvey out of the way. He's been the RB2, RB9 and RB7 in usage most recently. Look at the names he's next to here:

The matchup is far more difficult this week, however, after beating up on the Panthers and Raiders. The Steelers are a full tier above those DLs, even if they are pretty banged up at the moment. They haven't allowed a 100-yard back in more than six weeks. Saquon Barkley (RB13) and Chase Brown (RB6) scored their way to nice games most recently, for what it's worth. Denver has a 20.25-point team total (21st).

8. Cam Skattebo (at IND)

Skattebo dominated touches again. He had 14 carries and seven targets in an upset win against the Jaguars, leading to 17.0 expected half PPR points. Despite fumbling in the second half, the Giants stuck with him and he ultimately closed the game out with a backflip. It's almost as simple as they don't want Devin Singletary on the field anymore, which means Skattebo should float to some nice RB1/2 weeks.

The bad news is his tape last week was pretty rough, as was J.J. McCarthy's. They won't face a loaded Jaguars defense every week, but Skattebo is at risk of being benched if he continues to put the ball on the dirt. His range of outcomes remains wide, but there is clear upside if he can keep it together.

This is a matchup to feel confident in with the Colts very clearly tanking. They've allowed 26.5 half PPR points to RB rooms over their past four games, on 152 rushing YPG. David Montgomery had 124 total yards, Ollie Gordon had 115, Javonte Williams had 124 and Bhayshul Tuten had 159. This is a blowup spot with the Giants projected for 24.0 points.

9. Bijan Robinson (at MIN) - 97.5 proj. total yards

I'm afraid a real reset is due. Bijan has been the RB11 on RB10 usage over the past month, sinking against the 49ers (RB19) and Bucs (RB28) with Michael Penix forgetting how to play QB. He's still handling a major workload and is too good not to have huge games down the stretch, but the Falcons did trade away their starting C and really struggling on defense, too.

This week, the Falcons are firmly in the "mid" quadrant. They're projected for just 17.5 points (28th) as touchdown dogs to the Vikings. Minnesota is obviously one of the best defenses, even if the Niners did whatever they wanted to last week. Penix's pressure panic could derail the entire offense if they aren't prepared. The plan will be to run the ball against them while they can, but hopefully it's not just a punt fest. The Vikings have recently faced a bunch of fantasy RB1s; Christian McCaffrey (RB15), James Cook (RB7), Jahmyr Gibbs (RB5) and Jonathan Taylor (RB8). Taking the average of that group would be an optimistic angle, as Atlanta is nowhere near as good as those offenses.

10. Chuba Hubbard (at TB) - 92.5 proj. total yards

Fantasy's MVP (Most Valuable Pick) without a doubt. Hubbard is the RB4 on RB4 usage this year, and the Panthers have rode him extra hard this past month (RB1 overall usage). He's the only stable part of their offense.

The Buccaneers represent the league's toughest positional test on paper, ranking 32nd in half PPR points allowed to RBs at 14.8 per game. Opposing backfields generate just 9.8 rushing points per game against Tampa Bay (29th), though Jahmyr Gibbs did post an RB3 finish against them in Week 11 in what I'd call a true bat fight. Hubbard was held to 60 scoreless yards in Week 7 and hasn't finished better than RB24 against them since Week 13 of 2023. Carolina heads on the road as 3-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 20.25 points (21st). Without question, this is a difficult spot.

11. Bhayshul Tuten (vs. TEN)

We'll see if he's going to keep playing through this ankle/foot injury. Make sure Chris Rodriguez Jr. is picked up just in case. More later.

12. D'Andre Swift (at DET) - 74.5 proj. total yards

Swift had a rough game on tape and lost meaningful touches to others in the backfield. He bounced a zone run that should've been cut back, then proceeded to fumble. He didn't return after that rep in the fourth quarter. That said, the Kyle Monangai tape was lackluster, too. He's not 100% on his right toe injury and will have a short week with Thanksgiving here. The assumption is Swift starts, leads the backfield and doesn't have the RB1 role he had without Monangai. Since Week 5 of last year, Swift is the RB14 on RB16 usage. He was the RB16 on RB16 usage last week. View him as a boom-bust RB2.

The Lions defense is going to miss DE Aidan Hutchinson and LB Jack Campbell, though they still have some physical DEs and star DTs to worry about up front. Across the year, the Lions are fourth-best against fantasy RBs, but with the recent injuries and the fact that the Bears can stay in positive game scripts, this Lions defense seems more vulnerable than the spreadsheets would indicate. They have put a lid on Swift's fantasy value in recent matchups, for what it's worth, as Swift has mounted 48, 69, 53 and 74 yards, respectively, against them since 2024. A massive 29.0-point team total (third) is the most important mark, however. There is plenty of upside.

13. Kyren Williams (vs. GB) - 80.5 proj. total yards

Williams has had his two worst fantasy games of the year in back-to-back weeks. In Week 10 before the bye, Blake Corum outclassed him as a ball carrier, simply showcasing more short-area burst while offering the same high-level vision. The Rams also made sure to say Williams has a "sore toe", which, in a worst-case scenario, would be a turf toe. That's a terrible injury for a RB to try to play through. We're finally at the point that Corum has a chance to steal more carries from Williams, who is likely to remain the favorite in the pass game if the Rams are ever trailing. Even over this "bad" month stretch, Williams is the RB17 in expected half PPR points.

The Packers have been run on at times, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to RBs. They're on a 6-game stretch of allowing a top-20 fantasy RB and have missed LB Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles). We'll see if Micah Parsons (ACL) is playing, as expected. While 3-point favorites, the Rams "only" project for 23.75 points (12th) this week. Williams is a suddenly volatile fantasy RB2.

14. Blake Corum (vs. GB) - 71.5 proj. total yards

To my eyes and the spreadsheet's charts, Corum is a better rusher than Kyren Williams, who is reportedly dealing with a "sore toe" coming out of the bye. It'd be a bit of a surprise if Corum was the early-down starter, but I'm open to it happening for the first time ever. Corum won't have the pass-game value that Williams has shown off, but he's still the RB12 on RB20 usage this past month with the offense losing Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. They really need the Corum explosive runs to keep the offense alive.

The Packers have been run on at times, allowing the sixth-most fantasy points to RBs. They're on a 6-game stretch of allowing a top-20 fantasy RB and have missed LB Edgerrin Cooper (Achilles). We'll see if Micah Parsons (ACL) is playing, as expected. While 3-point favorites, the Rams "only" project for 23.75 points (12th) this week. Corum can be viewed as a fantasy RB2 in the same tier as Williams.

15. Breece Hall (at MIA) - 78.5 proj. total yards

Hall played on 5-of-6 snaps inside the 10-yard line last week, so it's not as cut-and-dry as Braelon Allen is The Biggest, The Largest and will be subbed in for all red-zone work. Since returning from injury, Hall is the RB13 on RB15 usage. He had his best game last week in a win, while finishing as an RB2/FLEX in losses to the Chiefs and Bills. The Jets want to run the ball as much as they can, but the game script will need to cooperate to pull that off.

Enter the Dolphins. The Jets are favored, and Miami has allowed the 7th-most fantasy points to RBs this year. They've also recently placed three key DTs on injured reserve. James Cook just finished as the RB10 against them last week, and they've been on a 6-game streak of allowing at least one RB to finish as a top-24 back. It's a good spot of course.

16. Saquon Barkley (at DAL) - 76.5 proj. total yards

We'll see if Barkley is going to play after his second stinger of the season last week ...

Barkley hit the gas last week and still looks like one of the best backs on tape. That's the good news. The problem is he was still only the RB13 on RB21 usage, without a reception, in an offense that is absolutely stuck with bad QB play. He only played 64% of the snaps coming out of the bye, losing some pass-game work to Will Shipley. He'll need a big play and some infrequent goal-line scores to hold the line as a fantasy RB2. He's the RB19 on RB36 usage since returning. Consider that his low-end baseline.

The reason for hope here is the Cowboys defense. They were hilarious against the Titans last week and have allowed the most fantasy points to RBs (25.7 half PPR per game) throughout the year on the most rushing yards per game (152). It's somehow been worse over their past month (31.1 PG). Barkley had a couple of impressive reps when returning from injury against them in Week 7 (RB20 on RB32 usage) and is in a better spot now. Philadelphia enters the holiday matchup as 8.5-point road underdogs with an implied total of 19.5 points (23rd). He has to take over for the Eagles to pull off the upset.

17. Jonathan Taylor (vs. NYG)

There's a ton going on. The Colts releasing Daniel Jones for Anthony Richardson Sr. is a slight negative for Taylor, as ARich is more likely to score near the goal line and less likely to maintain long drives. Indianapolis also didn't have its starting OTs last week (and of course, it traded LG Quenton Nelson) and Richardson's play under pressure is concerning. That's something very much worth tracking. As a reminder, here are Taylor's historical splits based on how many points Indy scores:

Jonathan Taylor fantasy points since 2021:
+ Colts score 0-17 ➡️ 11.3 half PPR (RB18)
+ Colts score 18-24 ➡️ 14.9 (RB15)
+ Colts score 25-30 ➡️ 19.7 (RB3)
+ Colts score 31+ ➡️ 29.5 (RB1)

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 10, 2026

The Colts project for 17.5 here.

The good news for Taylor's RB2 value is Seth McGowan (hamstring) is "going to miss some time." Over the past month, McGowan has stolen real work from Taylor before garbage time. That's included some red-zone scores, and I totally get why they were doing that, as McGowan was running well. They'll stop rotating Taylor out now. Over the past month, Taylor has been the RB52 (!!!) on RB16 usage. We're back to having hope for an RB15 on RB10 usage finish.

The matchup is daunting. The Giants suffocate games on both sides with a balanced offense and a hard-hitting defense. They upset the Jaguars last week, holding Bhayshul Tuten to just 53 yards. Ditto to the Commanders RBs in Week 10 and Saquon Barkley in Week 9. On the whole, New York is averaging just 16.6 half PPR points to RB rooms (27th).

18. Chase Brown (vs. NO)

That was a painful primetime game from Brown, who dropped multiple targets and took 6 carries for just 6 yards. He's the RB21 on RB15 usage this season, as one of the most inefficient players with the context of how great this Bengals offense is. I'm not sure if he's even better than Samaje Perine, who is one of the most underrated insurance options as we close out the fantasy season. This offense gives Brown multi-score upside as we saw in Week 10, but those were out of structure receiving touchdowns. Perine threatens at the goal line and now in the 2-minute drill. He's a volatile fantasy RB2, as he's been throughout the year. Brown is leading the position in receptions per game (5.2).

The Saints offer one of the friendliest matchups in football, ranking 2nd in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 25.6 points per game. New Orleans ranks 3rd in rushing points allowed (18.4 per game) and 8th in receiving points allowed to the position, having recently surrendered big games to Chuba Hubbard (RB4) and Jaylen Warren (RB17). Cincinnati features the league's highest neutral pass rate at 67% (1st) and enters as 10-point home favorites with an implied total of 30.75 points (2nd).

19. Tony Pollard (at JAX) - 79.5 proj. total yards

Pollard has been carrying the Titans offense, one that is playing at the league's fastest pace over the past month to better fit Cam Ward's chaotic skillset. More play volume is always welcomed for fantasy. Pollard has been the RB3 on RB7 usage over that stretch, handling 19.0 carries and 3.5 receptions per game. Tyjae Spears is on IR, so it's strictly Pollard until absolute garbage time. At any point, the Titans can completely disintegrate on offense without LG Peter Skoronski. He's best viewed as fantasy RB2 even if the results have been better than that of late.

The Jaguars have an awesome defense. Pollard broke a few tackles on a checkdown for a long score against them two games ago, finishing as the RB8 on RB12 usage. That's as good of an outcome as we can hope for. Since then, they've added two quality starters, including run-stopping DT Jordan Davis. Across the year, Jacksonville has allowed the 3rd-fewest fantasy points to RBs (15.1 half PPR per game). Pollard was the RB25 and RB47 against them last year, and they haven't allowed a 100-yard RB this season and only two have cleared 14 carries. Opposing backfields muster just 8.7 rushing fantasy points per game (30th) against the Jaguars, prompting offenses facing them to pass at a 59% rate in neutral scripts (second-highest). Tennessee travels as 14.5-point road underdogs with a slate-low implied team total of 16.5 points (32nd).

20. Ashton Jeanty (at CLE)

Jeanty had his best fantasy outing since Week 1, based on two explosive plays. He went untouched for 46 yards up the gut when the LB and S got washed up, and then he ran a wheel route against part-time OLB Quandarrius Robinson for a long score. It's awesome that this happened, but if we're being honest, he had a lot of daylight on each of them.

The good news is he still had 15.8 expected half PPR points (RB10) with five receptions while splitting carries fairly evenly with Mike Washington Jr. Jeanty has come out of the absolute bottom of his workload and looks healthy. We'll see if he can create more plays down the stretch as a boom-bust fantasy RB2. He's the RB17 on RB11 usage this year now.

21. Jaylen Warren (vs. DEN) - 78.5 proj. total yards

Last week was a nightmare game. There weren't many lanes on film review, and he couldn't bring in what could've been a 31-yard receiving TD on a ball that was a bit high on Aaron Rodgers. Beyond that, the Steelers were trailing, which meant Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for just five touches in the second half. Across the entire season, Warren is averaging 2.6 expected half PPR points fewer in games with Dowdle at this point, on 4.0 fewer carries and 1.2 fewer targets per game. Warren is back to being a firm fantasy RB2.

The matchup is one that comes with some advantages and some weaknesses. The Broncos have a strong DL, one that will put pressure on their backup LG. Denver also has very concerning LB play, while having standouts at all corner spots. The ball typically gets funneled to RBs against the Broncos, who are allowing the ninth-most fantasy points to the position on 126 rushing yards per game (10th). Ashton Jeanty popped up for 169 total yards last week, while Chuba Hubbard (96) and Emmett Johnson (143) hit them hard in the outings before that. The Steelers only project for 17.25 points (30th), so the lack of floor is alarming.

22. Quinshon Judkins (vs. LV) - 62.5 proj. total yards

Judkins is the RB23 on RB25 usage since pass-catching backup Dylan Sampson has returned to the lineup. Judkins' receiving role has been bad over the past month (1.8 receptions per game), so he's entirely touchdown dependent as a FLEX option. The good news is his workload is pretty stable, putting up between 10.7 and 12.6 expected half PPR points in five-straight games.

The Raiders rank 4th in half PPR points allowed to running backs, yielding 24.6 points per game. That vulnerability is almost entirely on the ground, where Las Vegas ranks 1st in rushing points allowed to backs (19.5 per game), compared to ranking 28th against receiving backs. That's okay for Judkins!!! Jonah Coleman (RB1) and Braelon Allen (RB7) each posted top-10 finishes against them recently. Cleveland sits as 4.5-point home favorites with an implied total of 23.0 points (15th).

23. Derrick Henry (at HOU)

The last two games with Jacoby Brissett have been totally fine. He's been the RB9 and RB12 on RB12 and RB11 usage. That's a good baseline for him moving forward, but we'll have to adjust for matchup as those games were close games against the Chargers and Panthers. He's catching more passes in an offense that will add 10+ dropbacks per game versus previous versions of this offense. That will offset the potential drop in goal line scores.

Houston ranks 19th in half PPR points allowed to running backs this season (18.5 per game), including a 20th-place ranking in rushing fantasy points surrendered to the position. The Texans recently held Jonathan Taylor to an RB33 finish in Week 11 after yielding an RB15 showing to Quinshon Judkins in Week 10. They won't have LB Azeez Al-Shair but have a strong DL still. Baltimore enters as 6.5-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 20 points (22nd).

24. Ollie Gordon (vs. NYJ) - 89.5 proj. total yards

Gordon is the RB16 on RB18 usage since being the Dolphins' starter, but the wind is coming out of the sail right now. He's down to the RB41 on RB27 usage this month with the offense losing Malik Willis. He's been the RB18 and RB24 over the past two weeks with Kyle McCord, and one of those was a Colts' game. It'll be hard for Gordon to see 16+ carries if the Dolphins are trailing early.

The Jets rank ninth in half PPR points allowed to running backs at 21.9 points per game. New York has surrendered heavy production on the ground, ranking 8th in rushing points allowed to backs, and gave up an RB1 finish to Kenneth Walker III and an RB7 finish to James Cook over their last four games with DT T'Vondre Sweat on IR. Gordon posted 16.8 half PPR points on 25 carries against them back in Week 7. Miami enters as 3.5-point home underdogs with an implied team total of 18.5 points (26th).

25. Jacory Croskey-Merritt (at ARI)

Croskey-Merritt returned from injury and was the Commanders' go-to option right away. They demoted Rachaad White to distant third duties, while Austin Ekeler spelled Bill. He ended up as the RB12 on RB17 usage in a close upset win. He handled the lone inside the five-yard line opportunity and offers the most juice on the ground. He can be phased out as a forgettable receiving option, but when the Commanders are rolling, he can get hot.

Well, Arizona up next! The Cardinals allow 20.8 half PPR points per game to running backs (12th-most), including 14.4 points per game specifically on the ground (13th). Arizona has surrendered big yardage and scoring on the ground recently, including Emmett Johnson (RB6) posting 105 rushing yards and a score in Week 11 and Blake Corum (RB9) gaining 100 yards and a touchdown in Week 10. Washington heads out as seven-point road favorites with a 23.75-point implied team total (13th).

26. Aaron Jones Sr. (vs. ATL) - 47.5 proj. total yards

Jones is only the RB45 on RB50 usage in 6 games with Jordan Mason, but Kirk Cousins is here to save the day. Over the past two weeks, Jones is the RB20 and RB19 on RB14 and RB35 usage. Cousins is willing to check the ball down, plus is going to sustain more drives than what Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz were able to do earlier on. Jones is still mixing in the occasion touchdown despite being the smaller back.

The Vikings are in a better spot this time around. They're touchdown favorites to the Falcons, who were smoked by Emmett Johnson last week (171 total yards). Bucky Irving (170) and Christian McCaffrey (100) were also top-10 backs against them this month. Across the entire season, Atlanta is allowing the 5th-most fantasy points to RBs. There is far more FLEX appeal this time around than in previous weeks. A 24.75-point team total (9th) backs that up.

27. David Montgomery (vs. BAL)

Montgomery is going back to a split backfield with Wood Marks expected to clear the concussion protocol, so we can largely through last week's predictable solid outing (RB13 on RB6 usage) against the tanking Colts. In Weeks 1-4 with Marks, Montgomery was the RB23 on RB30 usage. He lit up the Bills in Week 1, then was the RB47, RB36, and RB45 in the following games. I thought Marks was out-playing him on tape. After last week's clean outing, it'll be Monty as the starter and lead back most likely. Unfortunately, if it's somewhere around a 60/40 split, then it's harder to make the math work. The Texans' RB room is averaging 18.0 expected half PPR points, and their efficiency is almost always bad.

The good news is the Texans have found a grove on offense with C.J. Stroud throwing the ball well with a deep WR room. Houston owns a 26.5-point team total as big favorites to the struggling Ravens. Baltimore was gashed by Chuba Hubbard (RB2), Omarion Hampton (RB11), Chris Rodriguez (RB18) and James Cook (RB13) over the past month, leading to the 7th-most points over that span. Montgomery has fart into the end zone hope here. He's a solid FLEX.

28. Zach Charbonnet (at SF) - 71.5 proj. total yards

Charbonnet has been the RB39, RB22 and RB24 since returning from a torn ACL. He had the bye week to get his legs back under him, though that also plays into Post-Bye Rookie Bump Jadarian Price. They've split the workload in fairly predictable ways. Charbonnet is going to handle most of the goal-line and short-yardage carries, while Price is going to be designed a couple of targets and given some perimeter runs to take advantage of his better speed. The Seahawks are a balanced offense, so either one can have a random big game. For the most part, Charbonnet is not a big-play threat, so his role is far more touchdown-dependent.

The 49ers rank 25th in half PPR points allowed to opposing backfields at 16.8 per game, presenting a split matchup profile. San Francisco has been stout against pure ground work, sitting 31st against RB rushing (8.6 points per game allowed), but ranks sixth-most favorable against RB receiving at 8.0 half PPR points per game. Bijan Robinson (RB19) managed five receptions for 59 yards against them in Week 7, while Ashton Jeanty (RB43) was limited to 25 rushing yards on six carries in Week 9. Seattle enters as three-point road underdogs with an implied team total of 22.25 points (16th).

29. Rhamondre Stevenson (at LAC) - 65.5 proj. total yards

The Patriots are turning to Tommy DeVito this week, immediately being faced with a 17.0-point team total (30th). It's fair to say full adjustments are needed, even if TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is on IR and may not play again this year. Stevenson was phased out of the game in Germany before this bye, but hopefully he's fresher now. He'll split time with early-down option Corey Kiner. The matchup is just fine. The Chargers are middle of the back in all defensive metrics.

Unfortunately, we're in the Wild West for Stevenson's fantasy value. He's at the mercy of just how bad the QB play will be moving forward. We're probably at the point where the savior is Daniel Jones in a week or so. Never a good spot to be in.

30. Kaleb Johnson (at LAR) - 35.5 proj. total yards

Josh Jacobs (finger) will miss, leaving the Packers with Johnson and Marshawn Lloyd on the ground, with Chris Brooks in for pass protection. To me, Johnson is just way better than Lloyd as a rusher. The Packers seem to agree. He was the one to lead the backfield in carries in Week 10 without Jacobs, and there's no reason to believe he won't see 10-15 carries off the bye. Johnson is the RB26 on RB40 usage since Week 9 while facing the Patriots and Vikings.

The Packers will be challenged by a Rams' veteran-filled DL fresh off the bye. Los Angeles is the second-best defense against fantasy RBs this year, completely shutting out bad run games of late (ARI, WAS, LAC, LV, ARI). James Cook III was able to post 118 total yards against them in Week 5, at least. Johnson is a red-zone threat for a team projected for 20.75 points on Thanksgiving. He's a half-PPR FLEX.

31. Travis Etienne Jr. (at CIN)

We'll need two more data centers to figure out how Etienne wasn't able to score on his 46-yard run last week:

Etienne disproving geometry theorems pic.twitter.com/47dYFVHtgY

— Hayden Winks (@HaydenWinks) November 23, 2026

I can't say his tape has looked very good since returning, but the Saints are at least committing to him on the ground with Audric Estimé healthy-scratched. Etienne was the RB23 on RB18 usage, ceding all receiving work to protector C.J. Donaldson and Alvin Kamara. That puts a firm lid on his fantasy value, especially while the OL has backups at C and RT. He'll need a TD to pay off as a FLEX play. Last week, Kamara subbed in for a designed receiving touchdown near the goal line.

32. Omarion Hampton (vs. NE)

Hampton had another solid game, as the Chargers were at least able to keep the game close. It's clear that when Hampton is in, they're going to call a bunch of pitches at this point. He took one for 36 yards off the edge this week. He's still not trusted in the passing game and lost plenty of snaps to Kimani Vidal this past week. Still, Hampton being the RB18 on RB25 usage is a win. Over the past month coming out of the bye, Hampton is the RB38 on RB33 usage. He's very game-script dependent.

33. Braelon Allen (at MIA) - 55.5 proj. total yards

34. Kyle Monangai (at DET) - 42.5 proj. total yards

Monangai only had eight carries in his return from turf toe. I went into his tape not knowing which foot had the injury, but after the first few carries, I was able to figure that out (and was correct after looking it up). His right side is bugging him, and it's coming through when he's trying to cut on it. Monangai is simply not near 100% health. He'll have a short week to get right for Thanksgiving, but that's asking for too much. It's more likely that the Bears keep him in a more part-time role. He was the RB32 in usage last week with six teams on bye as a forgettable FLEX option.

At least Monangai has a clean matchup with the Lions on deck. They've been very strong against fantasy RBs throughout the season, but they're without DE Aidan Hutchinson and LB Jack Campbell right now. Bucky Irving had 100 yards, plus an 80-yard score called back against them last week. The markets agree that it's a soft matchup, as Chicago has an impressive 29.0-point team total (third) on Thanksgiving. Hoping for a touchdown in this offense isn't the worst fantasy idea.

35. Jordan Mason (vs. ATL) - 64.5 proj. total yards

36. Samaje Perine (vs. NO)

Are we sure he’s worse than Chase Brown? I view Perine as one of the best insurance backs in fantasy down the stretch. Add him now.

37. Jadarian Price (at SF) - 40.5 proj. total yards

38. Kenneth Gainwell (vs. CAR) - 37.5 proj. total yards

39. Emmett Johnson (at BUF)

Update: Kenneth Walker (groin) was a DNP on Monday. EJ would be a top-4 play if he’s out again.

Johnson popped off for RB3 and RB6 finishes, respectively, as the interim starter, handling the usual Kenneth Walker III role. He reminds me of Bucky Irving in some ways, but there is still a physicality and long-speed gap to Walker. He'll return back to his part time role, perhaps with an extra handful of reps. His last three games with Walker were RB51, RB42 and RB57 in expected half PPR points. Graduating from that all the way up to the FLEX range is asking for a lot. That's especially true in the rare game where the Chiefs are underdogs.

40. Rico Dowdle (vs. DEN) - 40.5 proj. total yards

41. Chris Rodriguez Jr. (vs. TEN)

42. Alvin Kamara (at CIN)

43. Mike Washington (at CLE)

44. Dylan Sampson (vs. LV) - 47.5 proj. total yards

45. Woody Marks (vs. BAL)

46. Tyler Allgeier (vs. WAS)

47. Austin Ekeler (at ARI)

48. Justice Hill (at HOU)

49. Kaelon Black (vs. SEA) - 33.5 proj. total yards

50. Corey Kiner (at LAC) - 29.5 proj. total yards

item.title: Detroit Lions lose another defender to season-ending injury
item.description: Detroit Lions rookie DT standout Skyler Gill-Howard is out for the year with a knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
The injuries to the Detroit Lions defense are starting to mount. On Tuesday, Lions coach Dan Campbell revealed that rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard is out for the rest of the season with a knee injury sustained during the team’s win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Campbell said the injury occured when Gill-Howard was in the game during a goal-line play on offense.

“Sky is out for the year. He’s out for the year. He had a knee injury that will require surgery. So he’ll be out,” Campbell said. “I hate that for him. He’s had a heck of a season up to this point.”

It’s the third significant injury to a Lions defender in the past four weeks, joining linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) and Aidan Hutchinson (torn ACL).

Gill-Howard, the team’s sixth-round pick this year, was one of the most pleasant surprises from Detroit’s defense this year. He’s played 316 defensive snaps through 10 games, tallying 2.0 sacks, six quarterback hits, and a tackle for loss.

His loss, combined with Hutchinson’s season-ending injury, leaves the Lions a bit shorthanded on the defensive line in terms of pass rushers, but Campbell said it is an opportunity for several players to step up in his absence.

“We still got Mac (Alim McNeill) , we’ve got Tyleik (Williams), we’ve got Levi (Onwuzurike), we’ve got (Tyler) Lacy who can play in there. It could be (Mekhi) Wingo. Could be Taki (Taimani), could be AK (Aidan Keanaaina). So we’ve got options there,” Campbell said. “But you hate to lose a player like him. He’s had a heck of a rookie season. We’ve mentioned this, but for a young guy, he’s a pro. He’s conscientious in what he did, just the right approach.”

item.title: Packers activate Micah Parsons to 53-man roster
item.description: Signs continue to point toward Parsons making his 2026 debut against the Rams on Wednesday night.
item.content:encoded:
The Packers have made it official — Micah Parsons is back on the roster.

Green Bay announced on Tuesday that Parsons has been activated to the 53-man roster in advance of Wednesday's game against the Rams.

Parsons has been medically cleared to play. While he's officially listed as questionable, all signs point to the edge rusher returning from his torn ACL this week in Los Angeles.

In 14 games for the Packers last year, Parsons tallied 12.5 sacks with 12 tackles for loss and 27 quarterback hits. He also had one pass defensed and two forced fumbles.

Though he wasn’t able to finish the 2025 season, he was still an AP first-team All-Pro for the third time in his career.

Green Bay had an open spot on its 53-man roster, so the club did not need to make a corresponding move.

item.title: Lions DT Skyler Gill-Howard out for season with knee injury
item.description: The Lions have lost another defensive player for the rest of the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
The Lions have lost another defensive player for the rest of the 2026 season.

Head coach Dan Campbell told reporters on Tuesday that defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard is going to miss the rest of the year. Gill-Howard has a knee injury that will require a surgical repair.

The Lions have also lost defensive end Aidan Hutchinson, linebacker Jimmy Rolder, and linebacker Jack Campbell in recent weeks.

Gill-Howard was a sixth-round pick in April and he appeared in all 10 games for the Lions this season. He had 11 tackles, two sacks, a tackle for loss and six quarterback hits.

item.title: Chris Jones says Chiefs’ No. 1 goal should be stopping James Cook
item.description: Kansas City has its sights set on the dynamic players in Buffalo’s backfield.
item.content:encoded:
When the Kansas City Chiefs’ defense lines up against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night, it will be the 1oth time Chiefs defensive tackle Chris Jones has been tasked with getting after Bills quarterback Josh Allen for four quarters, regular season and playoffs.

In those games, Jones has just one sack, three tackles for loss, eight quarterback hits, two passes defended and zero forced fumbles.

Through that experience, Jones has seen Allen grow into the elite signal caller he has become. On Tuesday, at the podium, he was asked about Allen’s game and where Jones has seen improvement in Buffalo’s leader.

“Just being more decisive, getting rid of the ball,” Jones shared. “I think his game has gotten better over the years, continuing to play at an MVP-level quarterback.”

Clearly, Allen has been hard to bring down throughout Jones’ chances at getting it done over the last six years. Jones pointed to former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger when describing how hard it is to tackle the 6-foot-5, 240-pound quarterback.

“It’s similar to Ben,” Jones pointed out. “He’s hard to bring down, and if you do get him in grips, he will switch the arm and throw it with his left arm. It’s so tough to bring a guy like him down, and I have such a deal of respect for how he plays the game and always in attack mode, so it’s always a competitive game.”

However, when thinking about Buffalo’s offense as a whole, Jones emphasizes running back James Cook, who has the second-most rushing attempts (209) and yards (1,060) in the NFL this season.

“Cook has been a dynamic force for them,” Jones noted. “He can break it at any moment. I think it’s an emphasis on stopping him, first and foremost. Try to contain Josh Allen, but mainly stopping him.”

“He’s such a dynamic back,” Jones continued. “He offers so many problems to many different levels whether it’s catching out of the backfield and running it, or cutting it back… I think the main goal, No. 1, is stopping Cook.”

Last year, Cook ran for 114 yards over 27 carries in a Buffalo victory — but that was the only time Kansas City has allowed the electric back to rush for over 100 yards on them.

item.title: Steelers Week 11 grades in loss to Eagles
item.description: Steelers Week 11 grades.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are now 6-4 following their second consecutive loss. As we do each week, Joey Bray and I will give our grades for the notable performances from Sunday. Let’s dive in.

QB Aaron Rodgers

Joey Bray: This was not Rodgers’ worst game of the season, but it was about what we have come to expect from Rodgers at this point. Despite being the team’s leading rusher, his mobility in the pocket was still quite poor as he took five sacks. Rodgers missed open receivers and passed up those who were often breaking open. If his name wasn’t Aaron Rodgers and this wasn’t a “last ride,” we would be having serious conversations about benching him. Grade: F

Jarrett Bailey: Guys are getting open, the quarterback is simply playing awful. Rodgers went into halftime averaging a mere half an air yard per attempt. He isn’t throwing downfield whatsoever, despite there being opportunities to do so, and at the slightest sense of pressure, he is checking the ball down. It’s unwatchable. Grade: D-

Run game

Joey Bray: The Steelers had one of the most efficient running games in the entire league through eight weeks. However, coming out of the bye, it has been the opposite. Pittsburgh posted just 73 rushing yards against an Eagles defense that came into the contest 25th against the run. A big part of their struggles could very well come from the absence of Mason McCormick, which spells disaster considering he is out for at least the rest of the regular season. What was once an elite Steelers run game has come to a screeching halt out of the bye and made their offense even more of a mess. Grade: F

Jarrett Bailey: It became evident how bad the Steelers miss Mason McCormick early on in the game. Spencer Anderson is a tire fire. He’s not an NFL capable player, and his incompetence led to the Steelers being completely unable to run the ball. Rodgers led the Steelers in rushing yards, which is how bad the ground attack was. Grade: F

Offensive line

Joey Bray: Spencer Anderson was already benched once this season, and it’s not hard to imagine it happens again given his performance in this one. Overall, allowing five sacks is never good, even when your quarterback is immobile. The run blocking now seems to be an issue as well. I’m willing to give them a bit of a break with the pass blocking considering the constant theme of quarterback immobility, but the run blocking is a major concern moving forward. Grade: D

Jarrett Bailey: Anderson was terrible, and Brock Hoffman wasn’t much better. The Steelers couldn’t run, and Rodgers was under pressure on 13 dropbacks. The offensive line crumbled when McCormick went down. They have to find someone else on that depth chart that can at least be serviceable. Grade: D-

WR Max Hurleman

Joey Bray: The undrafted wide receiver might have put together the best NFL debut of any Steelers skill position player since Antonio Brown returned a kickoff for a touchdown in his debut. Hurleman may not have had the impact on special teams that Brown did all those years ago, but he provided incredible value as a receiver. Hurleman is clearly someone that Rodgers trusts and capped his day off by scoring the Steelers’ only offensive touchdown. The Steelers should not take Hurleman off the field for the rest of the year given their struggles at receiver and return man this season. What a debut. Grade: A

Jarrett Bailey: Hurleman was the lone bright spot for the Steelers offense on Sunday. In his first taste of regular season action, he led the Steelers in receptions, yards, and touchdowns. He’s earned a helmet for the remainder of the year. Grade: A

Defense

Joey Bray: Once again, it was the Steelers offense that is taking most of the blame for the Steelers loss. It was not the best performance by the Steelers defense, but it was nowhere near last week’s blunder against the Bengals. It’s not like they got torched by Joe Milton or Saquon Barkley. Sure, the secondary once again showed how thin and depleted of talent they are, but you can’t ask for much more than allowing just 19 points to a team on their fourth quarterback of the season on the road. Grade: C

Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers’ defense did its job. They allowed just 214 yards of offense to the Eagles and just one touchdown. A free three points was gifted to Philadelphia when the Steelers turned the ball over on downs in their own territory to begin the game, and two of the other three field goals were from 50+ yards. This loss isn’t on the defense. Grade: B+

item.title: Ben Roethlisberger, Antonio Brown among former Steelers advancing in Hall of Fame voting
item.description: Six former Steelers are among the 52 nominees remaining for the Pro Football Hall of Fame class of 2027.
item.content:encoded:
Six former Steelers and one current Steelers coach are among the 52 former NFL players to advance in the Pro Football Hall of Fame’s voting process for the 2027 class.

Quarterback Ben Roethlisberger, wide receivers Antonio Brown and Hines Ward, defensive lineman LC Greenwood, outside linebacker James Harrison and center Maurkice Pouncey remain eligible for the class of 2027, the Hall of Fame announced Tuesday. Greenwood’s inclusion is because the Hall of Fame no longer differentiates between modern-era and senior candidates. Roethlisberger and Brown are in their first year of eligibility.

Former Saints offensive lineman and current Steelers assistant line coach Jahri Evans also advanced in the process for his career as a player.

Overall, 30 offensive players and 22 on defense remain in the nominee pool. Roethlisberger is among just three quarterbacks, along with Eli Manning and Ken Anderson. Other notable names — you can view the entire list here — include Rob Gronkowski, Adrian Peterson and Torry Holt.

According to the Hall of Fame’s website, the list of player nominees will next be narrowed down to 25 “in about the next two weeks.” Before the Super Bowl in February, 13 players, one coach and one contributor will be announced as finalists, with between three to seven eventually being voted into Canton.

item.title: NFL Playoff Picture: Which team is going to win the NFC East?
item.description: Probably not the Eagles.
item.content:encoded:
If you’re rooting for the Philadelphia Eagles to make the playoffs, the good news is that the Philadelphia Eagles did their part to keep extremely slim postseason hopes alive by beating the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The bad news is that every other team in the NFC East won in Week 11. And this despite two of those three being betting underdogs.

As such, the division standings now look like this entering Week 12:

1) New York Giants: 6-3-1
2) Dallas Cowboys: 5-6
3) Washington Commanders: 4-5-1
4) Philadelphia Eagles: 3-7

Can the Eagles make up a lot of ground in a short amount of time? Probably not! The betting odds to win the NFC East show that the Birds are massive long shots to threepeat as division champs:

  • Giants -230
  • Cowboys +410
  • Commanders +430
  • Eagles +12500

But if you’re building the case for optimism, it’s that the Eagles’ defense has stabilized over their past two games. Vic Fangio’s group limited the New York Giants to 19 points before holding the Pittsburgh Steelers to 16.

It’s difficult (read: nearly impossible) to feel good about the Eagles’ offensive outlook, especially after their lackluster performance against the Stillers. But at least they’re doing some different things stylistically? Maybe that leads to some positive results?

Again, probably not. But if there were a time for that much to happen, it would be against the Dallas Cowboys’ dreadful defense on Thanksgiving. If the Eagles can pull off an upset as 8.5-point road underdogs, they’re much more alive at 4-7 than they’d be at 3-8.

If we take the Eagles out of the equation, which is safe to do at this point in time, I’m curious to hear which team you think has the best chance of winning the NFC East. The Giants are in the top spot, yes, but they are set to face the NFL’s eighth-toughest remaining schedule and the Commanders hold a head-to-head tiebreaker over them. Washington also has the NFL’s third-easiest remaining schedule. The Cowboys’ offense is capable of staying hot down the stretch, though they have the ninth-toughest remaining schedule.

item.title: Bengals-Commanders clock error brings back memories of Steelers-Chargers clock error in 2015
item.description: Monday night's game between the Bengals and Commanders ended with an apparent error by the clock operator.
item.content:encoded:
Monday night's game between the Bengals and Commanders ended with an apparent error by the clock operator. The same thing happened eleven years earlier, on a Monday night in October.

The Chargers were hosting the Steelers. Here's the NFL’s official explanation, issued after the game:

"With 2:56 remaining in the fourth quarter, San Diego kicked off to Pittsburgh. The kick resulted in a touchback. By rule, the game clock does not start if the receiving team possesses the ball in the end zone and does not carry it into the field of play.

"Because of an error by the clock operator, the game clock was incorrectly started before the Steelers' first play from scrimmage following the touchback. That first down snap came with 2:38 left to play instead of 2:56, a difference of 18 seconds.

"The official game time is kept on the stadium scoreboard, but it is the responsibility of the side judge to supervise the timing of the game. Had the side judge or any of the other six on-field officials noticed the timing error, they could have corrected it.

"The game clock is not subject to instant replay review unless there is a timing issue on the last play of the first half or the last play of the game. The performance of the clock operator and game officials will be reviewed per the standard procedure for reviewing every play of every game."

The Steelers-Chargers situation shows that, when a clock error happens, the side judge becomes responsible for not catching it. On Monday night, that role was filled by Jimmy Buchanan. It was his job to ensure that the clock stopped when it was supposed to stop.

What comes next remains to be seen. In 2015, more than two years before the Supreme Court opened the floodgates for legalized gambling, the NFL interviewed the clock operator and side judge Rob Vernatchi.

The error in the 2015 game didn't impact the outcome; the Steelers won the game, 24-20. Vernatchi was nevertheless suspended for a week. The NFL thereafter implemented the "right controls" to keep it from happening again.

It apparently happened again on Monday night, based on the information ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk shared after the game. Time, pun intended, will tell whether the league acknowledges the error and imposes discipline and/or conducts a broader investigation.

item.title: Survey: Will the Giants put it all together against the Colts?
item.description: The NY Giants have been doing enough to win, but can they play a complete game against the Colts?
item.content:encoded:
The New York Giants are riding high after — once again — coming up with a win as underdogs. Very few people thought the Giants would beat the Jacksonville Jaguars, who are widely considered among the best and most complete teams in the NFL.

The most optimistic among us believed that there was a path for the Giants to come up with the win, but weren’t sure if they could execute. As it turned out, they did. They were able to do just enough on offense to establish a lead while their defense turned in a dominant performance for most of the game.

It was a great game by the Giants, but it wasn’t a complete game. The offense was still inconsistent and plagued by turnovers, miscues, and penalties. And while the defense was able to pick them up, they were gassed by the end of the game because the offense couldn’t sustain a drive after Cam Skattebo’s fumble.

The Giants’ win over the Jags is proving to be even bigger than anticipated, with the rest of the NFC East winning as well. That makes the upcoming game against the Indianapolis Colts into much more of a “must win” than it was before the Washington Commanders’ upset win over the Cincinnati Bengals. This is the time for the Giants to begin peaking if they want to be competitive in their upcoming games against the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Cleveland Browns, and Detroit Lions.

So this week we want to ask the Big Blue View community: Can the Giants put it all together and play a complete game against the Colts?

Your choices this week are:

A) Yes – The Giants’ offense and defense will play a complete 60 minute of football against the Colts.
B) No – The mistakes and miscues will return, but there will be marked improvement over previous weeks.
C) No – The offense is too mistake prone, with too many new players (J.J. McCarthy, Sisi Mauigoa, and Bryan Hudson), while the defense is just too injured, to play a complete game this year.
